questions.title: Hot key expiry takes down the database
questions.prompt: A product page cache entry with a 60 s TTL is read 40k times per second. Every minute, p99 latency spikes and the primary database CPU hits 100% for about 3 seconds. Which change fixes the root cause with the least new infrastructure?
questions.context:
```
12:00:00.012 cache MISS product:8812 (x 3,912 in 200ms)
12:00:00.240 db  pool exhausted (max=200)
```

options.text: Raise the TTL to 10 minutes so the miss happens less often
Coalesce concurrent misses so one request recomputes while the rest wait or serve stale
Add two read replicas behind the cache
Increase the connection pool size to 2,000

optionNotes.a: Spikes become rarer but just as large.
optionNotes.c: Spreads the herd but every replica still gets thousands of identical queries.
optionNotes.d: Moves the bottleneck into the database itself.

questions.explanation: This is a cache stampede: thousands of concurrent misses for one key. Request coalescing (single-flight), probabilistic early refresh or serve-stale-while-revalidate removes the herd. Longer TTLs and more capacity only change the size or frequency of the spike.
references: Vattani et al., Optimal Probabilistic Cache Stampede Prevention (VLDB 2015)

questions.title: Average write QPS for a check-in feature
questions.prompt: 50M daily active users each check in 2 times a day, spread evenly over the day. Roughly how many writes per second does that average out to?
questions.explanation: 100M writes / 86,400 s ≈ 1,157 writes/s. A useful shortcut: 1M per day ≈ 11.6 per second.

questions.title: Rename a column with zero downtime
questions.prompt: Put the steps for renaming `users.fullname` to `users.display_name` on a live service in order.

items.text: Deploy code that writes both columns

questions.explanation: Expand, migrate, contract: every step stays compatible with the code version before and after it, so any deploy can roll back.

questions.title: Global rate limiter for a public API
questions.prompt: Design a rate limiter that enforces 1,000 requests per minute per API key across 40 stateless API pods in two regions. Sketch the components and explain the algorithm and the failure behaviour.

keyPoints: Picks a concrete algorithm (token bucket or sliding window) and explains why
Keeps counters in a shared low-latency store, updated atomically (for example a Lua script or INCR with expiry)
Addresses cross-region: per-region budgets or async sync, with the accuracy tradeoff stated
Defines fail-open vs fail-closed when the counter store is down
Returns 429 with Retry-After and rate-limit headers
redFlags: A synchronous cross-region call on every request
rubric.exemplar: Gateway → rate-limit check against a regional Redis (sliding window counter via Lua, keyed by api key and minute) → service. Each region gets half the budget, rebalanced every few seconds. Redis down → fail open with a local token bucket as a coarse cap, and alert.

questions.explanation: Strong answers name the algorithm, the atomic shared counter, the cross-region accuracy tradeoff and the failure mode.

questions.title: Retry helper that hammers a struggling dependency
questions.prompt: This helper wraps calls to a payments API. During the last incident it made the outage worse. Find the bug.

issues.summary: Fixed 100 ms delay with no backoff or jitter, and every error is retried
issues.fix: Use exponential backoff with full jitter, cap total retry time, and only retry retryable errors (timeouts, 503, 429 honoring Retry-After).

questions.explanation: A constant short delay synchronizes every client into waves of retries that multiply load on a degraded dependency. Exponential backoff with jitter spreads them out; retry budgets cap amplification.
